content.text: The text combines several narratives. It recounts Sherman’s 1864 Atlanta Campaign: Johnston retreats from Dalton through Resaca, Cassville, Allatoona, New Hope, Kenesaw, and the Chattahoochee; Hood replaces him, attacks at Peach Tree Creek and Atlanta, and finally abandons Atlanta after Sherman cuts the Macon Railroad. Sheridan defeats Early at Winchester, Fisher’s Hill, and Cedar Creek. Grant surrounds Petersburg, fails at the Crater, then breaks Lee’s lines at Five Forks, forcing the evacuation of Richmond and Lee’s surrender at Appomattox. Sherman later marches from Atlanta through Georgia to Savannah, then through the Carolinas, defeating Johnston at Bentonville. Other passages describe Latin Quarter life, a comic domestic misunderstanding involving babies, goose-rearing practices, and Cyril Crichton’s discovery that his cousin Lord Wilmersley has been murdered at Geralton Castle. Cyril believes the missing Lady Wilmersley may be the woman he rescued. He travels to Geralton, investigates the swimming bath, library, bedrooms, and servants’ quarters, and consults detective Judson. A missing maid, Priscilla Prentice, may have helped Lady Wilmersley escape. The inquest examines Mustapha, Valdriguez, and reports of a motor-car near the castle.
